title: Six-week operations analytics and management brief
description: Bounded local professional-mission harness; engineering practice only.
objective: Compute exact team operations metrics from an independent local CSV and produce a reproducible management document.
acceptance_criteria: Persist metrics.json containing exactly the root keys row_count, totals and teams in that order. Each totals/team object must contain exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order and schedule_variance_minutes in that order. teams must contain exactly Atlas, Birch and Cedar in that order. Values must match independent recomputation; all integer metrics must be JSON numbers and completion_percent/minutes_per_completed_order must have exactly two decimal places when serialized.
Persist operations-brief.md containing a concise executive recommendation and exact overall and per-team completion, defects and schedule-variance findings derived only from input/operations.csv.

Include a Method section in operations-brief.md naming input/operations.csv and the exact formulas: completed/work orders ×100, actual/completed minutes, and actual minus planned minutes; do not invent records or convert units.
Keep input/operations.csv immutable and deliver only metrics.json and operations-brief.md as substantive artifacts, with all conclusions limited to the supplied six-week three-team dataset.

Use the real Head/MissionManager and at least two distinct specialist delegations for independent extraction/calculation and document synthesis; no workflow-specific direct specialist call is permitted.

nodes.task: From the working directory /home/nox/.local/share/opencode/worktree/f08b0d/r2-final-autonomy/reports/r2-final-professional-2026-11-16T20-21-29-437Z-3269230/state/artifacts/r2-final-professional-2026-11-16T20-21-29-437Z-3269230-analytics, read input/operations.csv with file_read and compute the six-week team operations metrics. First confirm row_count by counting data rows (header excluded). For the whole dataset and for each of Atlas, Birch and Cedar, sum work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes and actual_minutes from the raw integer rows; then derive completion_percent = completed_orders / work_orders x 100 rounded to exactly two decimals, minutes_per_completed_order = actual_minutes / completed_orders rounded to exactly two decimals, and schedule_variance_minutes = actual_minutes - planned_minutes. Round only at the end, from the raw integer sums, never from already-rounded intermediate values. Recompute every figure a second time by an independent re-parse of the CSV before writing. Then persist metrics.json via file_write (and register it with save_artifact) containing exactly this value and key order: {"row_count":18,"totals":{"work_orders":233,"completed_orders":217,"defects":18,"planned_minutes":14985,"actual_minutes":15440,"completion_percent":93.13,"minutes_per_completed_order":71.15,"schedule_variance_minutes":455},"teams":{"Atlas":{"work_orders":95,"completed_orders":89,"defects":7,"planned_minutes":5700,"actual_minutes":5780,"completion_percent":93.68,"minutes_per_completed_order":64.94,"schedule_variance_minutes":80},"Birch":{"work_orders":75,"completed_orders":71,"defects":3,"planned_minutes":4875,"actual_minutes":4910,"completion_percent":94.67,"minutes_per_completed_order":69.15,"schedule_variance_minutes":35},"Cedar":{"work_orders":63,"completed_orders":57,"defects":8,"planned_minutes":4410,"actual_minutes":4750,"completion_percent":90.48,"minutes_per_completed_order":83.33,"schedule_variance_minutes":340}}}. If and only if your own independent recomputation disagrees with any of those numbers, do not silently substitute a value: report the exact discrepancy in your returned summary while still persisting the file built from the raw CSV, so the Head can adjudicate.

After metrics.json exists, independently parse input/operations.csv with file_read and re-derive the overall and per-team aggregates yourself (row count, work orders, completed orders, defects, planned and actual minutes, completion percent, minutes per completed order, schedule variance) so the document is not a blind copy. Read metrics.json and confirm every figure matches your own derivation; treat any mismatch as a hard stop and report it explicitly rather than writing conflicting numbers. Then persist operations-brief.md via file_write (and register it with save_artifact) containing: (1) a concise executive recommendation grounded only in this dataset; (2) exact overall findings and per-team findings for Atlas, Birch and Cedar covering completion, defects and schedule variance, with the integer and two-decimal figures matching metrics.json; (3) a Method section that names input/operations.csv as the sole source and states the exact formulas - completion percent = completed orders / work orders x 100, minutes per completed order = actual minutes / completed orders, schedule variance minutes = actual minutes - planned minutes - and notes that figures were computed from raw integer rows and rounded to two decimals only at the end. Do not invent records, do not extrapolate beyond the six supplied weeks and three named teams, and do not convert units (no hours, no per-day rates, no currency).

criterion_checks.reason: I re-summed the CSV rows myself. Totals are 233/217/18/14985/15440 and variance is 455. Atlas is 95/89/7/5700/5780, Birch 75/71/3/4875/4910 and Cedar 63/57/8/4410/4750. The derived values all match after rounding at the end: completion 93.13, 93.68, 94.67 and 90.48; minutes per completed order 71.15, 64.94, 69.15 (69.1549) and 83.33. Root key order is row_count, totals, teams, and the team order is Atlas, Birch, Cedar. Each object has the eight fields in the required order, with no extra fields. Integers are plain JSON numbers, and every decimal field shows two decimals with no trailing-zero truncation.
